copy.en:
Did all the continents used to be connected?

Yes! Millions of years ago, they formed one giant landmass called Pangaea, slowly drifting apart as the tectonic plates moved.
copy.tl:
Magkadikit ba dati ang lahat ng kontinente?

Oo! Milyon-milyong taon na ang nakalipas, bumuo sila ng isang malaking lupain na Pangaea, at dahan-dahang naghiwalay habang gumagalaw ang mga tectonic plate.
copy.bis:
Nagdikit ba kaniadto ang tanang kontinente?

Oo! Milyon-milyon ka tuig na ang milabay, nagporma sila og usa ka dako nga yuta nga Pangaea, ug hinay-hinay nga nagbulag samtang naglihok ang mga tectonic plate.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It means continents were once joined and slowly moved apart over millions of years.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and explain evidence that current continents are separate parts of what was a single continent millions of years ago
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the basic claim of continental drift (continents were once joined and moved apart). The competency requires identifying and explaining evidence for this claim (e.g., fossil, rock, or glacial evidence). No evidence is presented, so the card does not directly support the skill.

copy.en:
What is continental drift?

In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift! It means continents were once joined and slowly moved apart over millions of years.
copy.tl:
Ano ang continental drift?

Noong 1912, iminungkahi ni Alfred Wegener ang continental drift! Ibig sabihin, ang mga kontinente ay dating magkadikit at dahan-dahang naglayo sa paglipas ng milyon-milyong taon.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang continental drift?

Niadtong 1912, gisugyot ni Alfred Wegener ang continental drift! Ibig sabihin, ang mga kontinente kaniadto nagdikit ug hinay-hinay nga nagbulag sulod sa minilyon nga katuigan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ocean-floor rocks are less than 200 million years old because tectonic processes continually create and destroy them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the location and distribution of active volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, and major mountain belts to the distribution of oceanic crust and continental crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oceanic and continental crust but focuses on their ages, not on relating the distribution of volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, or mountain belts to crust distribution. It shares vocabulary but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: because tectonic processes continually create and destroy them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to tectonic processes generally but does not describe structures, movements, or events at each type of plate boundary. It is background about crust age, not direct instruction for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Continental rocks can be over 4 billion years old! Ocean-floor rocks are less than 200 million years old
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how relative and absolute dating techniques are used to determine the subdivisions of geologic time
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives age comparisons but does not explain relative or absolute dating techniques or how they determine subdivisions of geologic time. The age facts are related content, not direct support for the dating-technique competency.

copy.en: Continental rocks can be over 4 billion years old! Ocean-floor rocks are less than 200 million years old because tectonic processes continually create and destroy them.
copy.tl: Ang continental rocks ay pwedeng mahigit 4 bilyong taon! Ang ocean-floor rocks ay wala pang 200 milyong taon dahil patuloy silang nililikha at sinisira ng tectonic processes.
copy.bis: Ang continental rocks mahimong kapin sa 4 ka bilyon ka tuig! Ang ocean-floor rocks ubos sa 200 ka milyon kay padayon kining gimugna ug gilaglag sa tectonic processes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the continents slowly drifted apart to where they are today
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and explain evidence that current continents are separate parts of what was a single continent millions of years ago
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that continents drifted apart due to plate movement, but it does not identify or explain any evidence (e.g., fossil, rock, or glacial evidence) that current continents were once a single landmass. It only mentions the general idea of continental drift.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because the plates move, the continents slowly drifted apart
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions plate movement causing continents to drift, but it does not describe the structures, movements, or events at any specific type of plate boundary (convergent, divergent, transform). It lacks the detail required by the competency.

copy.en: Because the plates move, the continents slowly drifted apart to where they are today!
copy.tl: Dahil sa galaw ng mga plaka, dahan-dahang naghiwalay ang mga kontinente patungo sa kinaroroonan nila ngayon!
copy.bis: Tungod sa lihok sa mga plaka, hinay-hinay nga nagbulag ang mga kontinente paingon sa ilang gitindogan karon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Millions of years ago, all continents were joined in one huge landmass called Pangaea!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and explain evidence that current continents are separate parts of what was a single continent millions of years ago
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the fact that continents were once joined as Pangaea, but the competency requires identifying and explaining evidence for this. No evidence is presented, so the card only touches the same topic without directly supporting the evidence-based skill.

copy.en:
Were all the continents always in the same place?

Millions of years ago, all continents were joined in one huge landmass called Pangaea!
copy.tl:
Nasa parehong lugar ba palagi ang mga kontinente?

Milyon-milyong taon na ang nakaraan, ang lahat ng kontinente ay magkadikit sa iisang malaking lupa na tinatawag na Pangaea!
copy.bis:
Kanunay ba sa parehong lugar ang tanang kontinente?

Milyon-milyon ka tuig na ang milabay, ang tanang kontinente nagkadikit sa usa ka dako nga yuta nga gitawag og Pangaea!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Convection happens only in liquids and gases!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the basic mechanism of convection (fluid movement carrying heat) but does not identify advantageous or disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, or radiation as required by the competency.

copy.en: Convection happens only in liquids and gases! The water or air itself must move to carry heat from one place to another.
copy.tl: Ang convection ay nangyayari lamang sa likido at gas! Kailangang gumalaw ang mismong tubig o hangin para dalhin ang init mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
copy.bis: Ang convection mahitabo lamang sa likido ug gas! Kinahanglan molihok ang mismong tubig o hangin aron madala ang init gikan sa usa ka dapit ngadto sa lain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a free ride from convection winds!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions land and sea breezes and calls them convection winds, but it does not explain how solar energy contributes to their occurrence, monsoons, or the ITCZ. It only gives a practical use of the breezes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fishermen used the land breeze before dawn to sail out to sea
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes wind moving boats, which is an example of natural causes moving objects, but it does not guide students to explore or demonstrate different ways to make objects move. It is an application, not instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a free ride from convection winds!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies breezes as convection winds, but it does not identify advantageous or disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation. It only labels the phenomenon as convection without comparing advantages or disadvantages.

copy.en:
How did old-time fishermen use the wind to sail?

Fishermen used the land breeze before dawn to sail out to sea, then caught the sea breeze in the afternoon to ride back to shore — a free ride from convection winds!
copy.tl:
Paano ginamit ng mga mangingisda noon ang hangin para maglayag?

Ginamit ng mga mangingisda ang land breeze bago madilim para lumayag papunta sa dagat, at ang sea breeze sa hapon para bumalik sa pampang — libreng sakay mula sa convection winds!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paggamit sa mga mananagat kaniadto sa hangin aron maglayag?

Gigamit sa mga mananagat ang land breeze sa kaadlawon aron maglayag padulong sa dagat, ug ang sea breeze sa hapon aron mobalik sa baybayon — libre nga sakay gikan sa convection winds!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That cool afternoon breeze at beaches like Batangas or Cebu? That's the sea breeze keeping you comfy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card names sea breeze as a phenomenon but does not explain how solar energy contributes to its occurrence. It provides no mechanism, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That cool afternoon breeze at beaches like Batangas or Cebu? That's the sea breeze keeping you comfy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: Sea breeze is a convection example, but the card does not identify it as convection nor discuss advantages/disadvantages of conduction, convection, or radiation. It only mentions a cool breeze without linking it to heat transfer concepts.

copy.en:
Why do beaches in the Philippines feel cool on hot afternoons?

The Philippines is made of islands, so almost everywhere is near the sea! That cool afternoon breeze at beaches like Batangas or Cebu? That's the sea breeze keeping you comfy!
copy.tl:
Bakit malamig ang hangin sa beach sa Pilipinas kahit mainit ang araw?

Ang Pilipinas ay kapuluan, kaya halos lahat ay malapit sa dagat! Ang preskong hangin sa hapon sa mga beach tulad ng Batangas o Cebu? Iyon ang sea breeze na nagpapakalma sa iyo!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga presko ang hangin sa baybayon sa Pilipinas bisan init ang adlaw?

Ang Pilipinas pundok sa mga isla, mao nga halos tanan duol sa dagat! Ang presko nga hangin sa hapon sa mga baybayon sama sa Batangas o Cebu? Kana ang sea breeze nga naghimo nimo komportable!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A microscope uses two convex lenses in a row!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions convex lenses, which are relevant to refraction, but it does not describe or illustrate reflection or refraction, nor does it explain how lenses bend light. It only states that a microscope uses two convex lenses to magnify, which is an application example but not direct instruction on the competency's core skill of describing/illustrating refraction with lenses.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A microscope uses two convex lenses in a row!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the parts and functions, and demonstrate proper handling and storing of a compound microscope
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the objective lens and eyepiece of a microscope, which are parts of a compound microscope, but it does not identify the parts and functions, nor demonstrate proper handling and storing. It only explains magnification by two lenses, which is background knowledge about how a microscope works, not the competency's focus on identifying parts/functions and handling/storing.

copy.en: A microscope uses two convex lenses in a row! The objective lens magnifies the image first, then the eyepiece magnifies it again, letting you see very tiny cells.
copy.tl: Ang mikroskopyo ay gumagamit ng dalawang convex lens! Pinapalaki muna ng objective lens ang larawan, tapos pinapalaki ulit ng eyepiece, kaya nakikita mo ang napakaliliit na selula.
copy.bis: Ang mikroskopyo naggamit og duha ka convex lens! Magpadako una ang objective lens, dayon magpadako pag-usab ang eyepiece, mao nga makita nimo ang gagmay kaayong selula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mirror that curves outward (convex) shows a wider area but makes things smaller — that's why it's used in car side mirrors and store corners to see more at once!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an everyday example of a convex mirror and its effect, but it does not involve carrying out a guided investigation, nor does it describe or illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors. It only mentions a use, which is a related application, not direct instructional support for the investigation-based competency.

copy.en:
Why do car side mirrors make everything look so tiny?

A mirror that curves outward (convex) shows a wider area but makes things smaller — that's why it's used in car side mirrors and store corners to see more at once!
copy.tl:
Bakit parang napakaliit ng lahat sa side mirror ng kotse?

Ang salamin na kurba palabas (convex) ay nagpapakita ng mas malawak na lugar pero mas maliit ang mga bagay — kaya ginagamit sa side mirror ng kotse at kanto ng tindahan!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga gamay tanan sa side mirror sa awto?

Ang salamin nga nagkurba pagawas (convex) magpakita og mas lapad nga dapit apan magpagamay sa mga butang — mao nga gigamit sa side mirror sa awto ug sa mga eskina sa tindahan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Convex mirrors are used as car side mirrors because they give you a wider view of the road!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a curved mirror (convex) and an everyday application, but it does not describe or illustrate reflection of light, nor does it support carrying out a guided investigation. It only states a use of a convex mirror without explaining the reflection principle.

copy.en: Convex mirrors are used as car side mirrors because they give you a wider view of the road!
copy.tl: Ginagamit ang convex na salamin sa gilid ng sasakyan dahil nagbibigay ito ng mas malawak na tanawin ng kalsada!
copy.bis: Ang convex nga salamin gigamit sa kilid sa sakyanan kay naghatag kini og mas luag nga panan-aw sa dalan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooking food with high heat kills many microbes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about heat killing microbes in food, not about factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions or their applications in food preservation, materials production, fire control, pollution, or corrosion. No chemical reaction rate concept is taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooking food with high heat kills many microbes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a change caused by temperature (heat), but it does not describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes, such as burning wood or coal. It is about microbial death, not material property changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooking food with high heat kills many microbes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It only states that high heat kills microbes, with no discussion of heat vs. temperature concepts.

copy.en: Cooking food with high heat kills many microbes, making your yummy meal much safer to eat!
copy.tl: Ang pagluto sa mataas na init ay pumapatay sa maraming mikrobyo, kaya mas ligtas kainin ang pagkain!
copy.bis: Ang pagluto sa taas nga init makapatay sa daghang mikrobyo, busa mas luwas kan-on ang pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oils have different smoke points! Coconut oil (177°C) is great for high-heat frying, while olive oil (160°C) is better for lower-heat cooking to avoid harmful breakdown products.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature-related behavior of oils (smoke points and breakdown products) but does not describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes as the competency requires; it is about choosing oils for cooking, not describing material property changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oils have different smoke points! Coconut oil (177°C) is great for high-heat frying, while olive oil (160°C) is better for lower-heat cooking to avoid harmful breakdown products.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on heating oils and breakdown products, but it does not explain why physical changes are reversible and chemical changes are irreversible. It provides no direct instruction on reversibility or irreversibility of changes.

copy.en:
Why use different oils for cooking?

Oils have different smoke points! Coconut oil (177°C) is great for high-heat frying, while olive oil (160°C) is better for lower-heat cooking to avoid harmful breakdown products.
copy.tl:
Bakit iba-iba ang langis na ginagamit sa pagluluto?

May iba't ibang smoke point ang mga langis! Ang langis ng niyog (177°C) maganda sa high-heat frying, habang ang olive oil (160°C) mas maganda sa lower-heat cooking para iwas harmful breakdown products.
copy.bis:
Nganong lahi-lahi ang langis sa pagluto?

Ang mga langis adunay lain-laing smoke point! Ang langis sa niyog (177°C) maayo alang sa high-heat frying, samtang ang olive oil (160°C) mas maayo sa lower-heat cooking aron malikayan ang harmful breakdown products.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Usually December to February!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions only the cool season (December to February) and does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities for each season. It shares vocabulary about seasons but does not directly support the competency's full scope.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: because of the cool amihan winds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the amihan winds as a cause of cool weather but does not explain how solar energy contributes to monsoons, land/sea breezes, or the ITCZ. It only names a wind, not the mechanism required by the competency.

copy.en:
When are the coolest months in the Philippines?

Usually December to February! We feel this chilly weather because of the cool amihan winds.
copy.tl:
Kailan ang pinakamalamig na panahon sa Pilipinas?

Karaniwang Disyembre hanggang Pebrero! Nararamdaman natin ang lamig dahil sa hanging amihan.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a ang pinakabugnaw nga panahon sa Pilipinas?

Kasagaran Disyembre hangtod Pebrero! Mabati nato ang tugnaw tungod sa hanging amihan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Freezing happens by decreasing the temperature of a liquid material until it hardens and changes into a solid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the phase change of freezing, which is unrelated to identifying evidence of global warming and climate change. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Freezing happens by decreasing the temperature of a liquid material until it hardens and changes into a solid.
copy.tl: Ang freezing ay nangyayari sa pamamagitan ng pagpapababa ng temperature ng isang liquid na materyal hanggang sa ito ay tumigas at maging solid.
copy.bis: Ang freezing mahitabo pinaagi sa pagpaubos sa temperature sa usa ka liquid nga materyal hangtod kini motig-a ug mahimong solid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When electricity flows through it, the coil acts like a magnet
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a current-carrying coil acts like a magnet, which is the basic idea behind an electromagnet, but it does not guide the student to make a simple electromagnet or to observe and record its properties as the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: making fans and toy motors spin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the similarities and differences between electric motors and electric generators
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions motors spinning but does not describe the similarities and differences between electric motors and electric generators, which is the required competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the coil acts like a magnet
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to a coil behaving like a magnet when electricity flows, but it does not support guided investigations to identify properties of magnets or how magnets affect other magnets and objects made of different materials.

copy.en:
How does copper make motors spin?

Copper wire is wound into a coil! When electricity flows through it, the coil acts like a magnet—making fans and toy motors spin!
copy.tl:
Paano ginagawa ng tanso na umikot ang mga motor?

Pinipilipit na paikot-ikot ang tansong wire para maging coil! Kapag dinaanan ng kuryente, nagiging parang magnet ito—kaya umiikot ang mga motor ng bentilador at laruan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa tumbaga nga molihok ang mga motor?

Giliko-liko ang tumbaga nga wire aron mahimong coil! Kung agian-an og kuryente, mahimo kining murag magnet—mao nga molihok ang motor sa bentilador ug dulaan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electricity flows in a loop around the circuit—the wire stays whole and safe.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a circuit loop and wire as a path, but it does not teach assembling or drawing a simple circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb/motor/buzzer, and no such representation is used.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Copper wire never gets used up by electricity! It's just a path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to copper wire as a conductor path, but it does not support designing/constructing a circuit to test which materials conduct electricity, nor identifying conductors and insulators from the environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Copper wire never gets used up by electricity! It's just a path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about electrical current flow and wire behavior in a circuit, not about matter having mass and taking up space. It does not support the matter competency.

copy.en: Copper wire never gets used up by electricity! It's just a path. Electricity flows in a loop around the circuit—the wire stays whole and safe.
copy.tl: Hindi nauubos ang tansong wire ng kuryente! Daanan lang ito. Dumadaloy ang kuryente nang paikot sa circuit—nananatiling buo at ligtas ang wire.
copy.bis: Dili maubos ang tumbaga nga wire sa kuryente! Agianan lang kini. Moagos ang kuryente og libot sa circuit—magpabilin nga buo ug luwas ang wire.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: copper was one of the very first metals people used to make tools and weapons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a historical use of copper (tools and weapons) but does not address properties of metals or uses by the local community as required by the competency. It shares the vocabulary 'copper' and 'metals' but provides no direct instructional support for identifying properties or local uses.

copy.en: Thousands of years ago, copper was one of the very first metals people used to make tools and weapons!
copy.tl: Libu-libong taon na ang nakalipas, ang tanso ay isa sa mga unang metal na ginamit ng tao para sa kasangkapan at sandata!
copy.bis: Liboan ka tuig na ang milabay, ang kobre usa sa unang metal nga gigamit sa tawo aron maghimo ug galamiton ug hinagiban!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it conducts electricity really well
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that copper conducts electricity well, which is a fact about a conductor, but it does not support the competency's action of designing and constructing a simple circuit to identify which materials conduct electricity. No circuit, testing procedure, or comparison of materials is provided.

copy.en:
Why do we use copper for electrical wires?

Copper is used because it is very affordable and it conducts electricity really well!
copy.tl:
Bakit ginagamit ang tanso sa mga kawad ng kuryente?

Ginagamit ang tanso dahil mura ito at napakahusay niyang ipadala ang kuryente!
copy.bis:
Nganong gigamit ang tumbaga sa mga kawad sa kuryente?

Gigamit ang tumbaga kay barato kini ug maayo kaayo niyang ipadala ang kuryente!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People press it to make coconut oil
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines copra and mentions pressing to make oil, but it does not describe how changes in solid materials make them useful (e.g., explaining the change process or its usefulness). The mention of pressing is incidental and not instructional for the competency.

copy.en:
What is copra?

Copra is the dried meat of the coconut. People press it to make coconut oil, one of the Philippines' important products to sell.
copy.tl:
Ano ang copra?

Ang copra ay ang pinatuyong laman ng niyog. Dito pinipiga ang langis ng niyog, isa sa mahahalagang produktong ipinagbibili ng Pilipinas.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang copra?

Ang copra mao ang pinauga nga unod sa lubi. Gikan niini ginapuga ang lana sa lubi, usa sa importante nga produkto nga gibaligya sa Pilipinas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It serves as both mouth and anus, ringed by tentacles that catch tiny prey
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: A mouth and tentacles are not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Just one! It serves as both mouth and anus, ringed by tentacles that catch tiny prey
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Polyp openings are not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en:
How many openings does a coral polyp have?

Just one! It serves as both mouth and anus, ringed by tentacles that catch tiny prey.
copy.tl:
Ilang butas lang ang meron ang coral polyp?

Isa lang! Ito ang parehong bibig at puwit nito, napapaligiran ng mga tentacle na panghuli ng maliliit na pagkain.
copy.bis:
Pila ka lungag ang naa sa coral polyp?

Usa ra! Kini ang parehong baba ug lubot niini, gilibutan sa mga tentacle nga panakop og gagmay nga prey.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it has a mouth in the middle ringed by little tentacles, and a hollow space inside works as its stomach
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: Mouth and tentacles are not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A coral polyp is like a tiny sac — it has a mouth in the middle ringed by little tentacles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Polyp body parts are not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en: A coral polyp is like a tiny sac — it has a mouth in the middle ringed by little tentacles, and a hollow space inside works as its stomach.

What is a coral's hard skeleton made of?

Hard corals build their tough skeleton from calcium carbonate — the very same mineral that makes up limestone rock.

Saan gawa ang matigas na kalansay ng coral?

Ang mga hard coral ay gumagawa ng matibay na kalansay mula sa calcium carbonate — ang parehong mineral na bumubuo sa apog o limestone.
copy.bis:
Unsa gama ang gahi nga kalansay sa coral?

Ang mga hard coral naghimo sa lig-on nga kalansay gikan sa calcium carbonate — mao rang mineral nga naghimo sa bato nga limestone.

copy.bis: Ang Cordillera sa amihanang Luzon usa ka dakong han-ay sa kabukiran ug puy-anan sa bantog nga hagdan-hagdan nga humayan!

copy.en:
Why do pilots and engineers watch out for the Coriolis effect?

They track the Coriolis effect on long airplane flights and rocket paths so they don't drift off target!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangang isaalang-alang ng mga piloto at inhinyero ang Coriolis effect?

Para hindi malihis sa target ang mga mahahabang paglipad ng eroplano at rocket!
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan tagdon sa mga piloto ug inhenyero ang Coriolis effect?

Aron dili masimang sa target ang tag-as nga paglupad sa ayroplano ug rocket!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do ocean currents curve as they flow?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ocean currents, which are bodies of water, but it does not identify local examples of landforms or bodies of water, nor does it describe how they influence living and non-living components. The Coriolis effect is not about the influence of landforms/water bodies on the environment.

copy.en:
Why do ocean currents curve as they flow?

Because Earth rotates! This makes currents curve right in the northern hemisphere and left in the southern, called the Coriolis effect.
copy.tl:
Bakit lumiliko ang mga agos ng dagat habang tumatawid?

Dahil umiikot ang Mundo! Kaya lumiliko pakanan ang agos sa hilagang globo at pakaliwa sa timog, tinatawag na Coriolis effect.
copy.bis:
Nganong magaliko ang mga sulog sa dagat samtang nagaagos?

Tungod kay nagatuyok ang Kalibutan! Mao nga magaliko patuo ang sulog sa amihanang bahin ug pawala sa habagatan, gitawag og Coriolis effect.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It only changes the direction of a moving object — not how fast it goes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that when forces are not balanced, they can cause changes in the object's speed or direction of motion
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the Coriolis effect changes direction but not speed. G7-F-4 requires identifying that unbalanced forces cause changes in speed or direction. The card does not mention forces, unbalanced forces, or the cause of the direction change; it only gives a fact about a specific apparent force. This is related vocabulary (direction change) but does not directly teach the competency's concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It only changes the direction of a moving object — not how fast it goes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: G4-F-5 is about demonstrating that pushes and pulls (contact forces) can change speed and direction. The card only mentions direction change, which is a shared word but not the competency's focus.

copy.en:
What does the Coriolis effect change about a moving object?

It only changes the direction of a moving object — not how fast it goes!
copy.tl:
Ano ang binabago ng Coriolis effect sa gumagalaw na bagay?

Binabago lang nito ang direksyon ng gumagalaw na bagay — hindi ang bilis nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang giusab sa Coriolis effect sa naglihok nga butang?

Mag-usab lang kini sa direksyon sa naglihok nga butang — dili sa kapaspas niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's named after Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis, a French scientist who described it in 1835!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only identifies the scientist after whom the Coriolis effect is named. It does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons, which are the actions required by G8-E-7. The Coriolis effect is a related concept but is not taught here.

copy.en:
Who is the Coriolis effect named after?

It's named after Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis, a French scientist who described it in 1835!
copy.tl:
Kanino ipinangalan ang Coriolis effect?

Ipinangalan ito kay Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis, isang Pranses na siyentista na naglarawan nito noong 1835!
copy.bis:
Kang kinsa ginganlan ang Coriolis effect?

Ginganlan kini sunod kang Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis, usa ka Pranses nga siyentista nga naghulagway niini niadtong 1835!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it also curves its whole path toward the north!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Coriolis effect curving a typhoon's track poleward. This does not explain how typhoons develop nor why the Philippines is prone to typhoons, which are the two required actions of G8-E-7. It only shares the general topic of typhoons.

copy.en: The Coriolis effect doesn't just make a typhoon spin — it also curves its whole path toward the north!
copy.tl: Hindi lang pinaiikot ng Coriolis effect ang bagyo — kinukurba rin nito ang buong landas nito papuntang hilaga!
copy.bis: Dili lang patuyokon sa Coriolis effect ang bagyo — mokurba usab kini sa tibuok agianan paingon sa amihan!

copy.tl: Ang berdeng dahon ng mais ay gumagawa ng sariling pagkain mula sa sikat ng araw — at ito ang nagiging matamis na butil sa busal!
copy.bis: Ang lunhaw nga dahon sa mais maghimo sa kaugalingong pagkaon gikan sa kahayag sa adlaw — ug kini mahimong tam-is nga mga lugas sa busal!

copy.bis: Ang coronary heart disease usa ka kondisyon diin ang mga coronary arteries nga nagdala ug oxygenated blood sa kasingkasing nabara o mokitid tungod sa natigom nga tambok nga mga sangkap.

How deep does the Cotabato Trench go?

It reaches a depth of more than 5,700 meters.

Gaano kalalim ang Cotabato Trench?

Umaabot ito sa lalim na mahigit 5,700 metro.
copy.bis:
Unsa kalawom ang Cotabato Trench?

Moabot kini sa kalawom nga kapin sa 5,700 ka metro.

copy.en:
Where can we find the Cotabato Trench?

The Cotabato Trench is found off the southwest coast of Mindanao, right along the beautiful Celebes Sea!
copy.tl:
Saan natin makikita ang Cotabato Trench?

Ang Cotabato Trench ay matatagpuan sa timog-kanluran ng Mindanao, nasa gilid ng magandang Celebes Sea!
copy.bis:
Asa makit-an ang Cotabato Trench?

Ang Cotabato Trench makit-an sa habagatang-kasadpan sa Mindanao, sa daplin sa nindot nga Celebes Sea!

copy.tl: Ang bulak ay halamang nagbubunga ng malambot na puting hibla — ang parehong hibla na ginagawang sinulid at tela!
copy.bis: Ang gapas usa ka tanom nga mamunga og humok, puti nga lanot — ang mao gihapong lanot nga himoon nga sinulid ug panapton!

copy.tl: Ang cotyledon ay ang seed leaf ng buto na may nakaimbak na pagkain para pakainin ang bagong sibol na halaman — hanggang sa kaya na nitong gumawa ng sarili nitong pagkain sa pamamagitan ng photosynthesis.
copy.bis: Ang cotyledon mao ang seed leaf sa liso nga adunay tinipigan nga pagkaon aron pakan-on ang bag-ong salingsing — hangtod nga makahimo na kini og kaugalingong pagkaon pinaagi sa photosynthesis.

copy.en:
Why do we cough and sneeze?

Coughing and sneezing are your body's way of forcing germs and irritants out of your nose and throat.
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo umuubo at bumabahing?

Ang pag-ubo at pagbahing ay paraan ng katawan para itaboy palabas ang germ at irita sa ilong at lalamunan.
copy.bis:
Nganong mag-ubo ug mabahin kita?

Ang pag-ubo ug pagbahaon mao ang paagi sa lawas sa pagpagawas sa mga kagaw ug irita gikan sa ilong ug tutunlan.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions tree rings, which relate to growth, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It focuses on a sampling technique, not on teaching growth as a characteristic.

Do scientists need to cut a tree to count its rings?

Nope! Scientists can read a living tree's rings by taking a thin core sample—no need to cut the whole tree down!
copy.tl:
Kailangan bang putulin ang puno para bilangin ang singsing nito?

Hindi pala! Kayang basahin ng mga siyentipiko ang mga singsing ng buhay na puno sa pamamagitan lang ng pagkuha ng manipis na sampol, hindi na kailangang putulin ito!
copy.bis:
Kinahanglan bang putlon ang kahoy aron maihap ang singsing niini?

Dili diay! Mabasa sa mga siyentista ang mga singsing sa buhi nga kahoy pinaagi lang sa pagkuha og nipis nga sampol, dili na kinahanglan putlon kini!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves counting seconds and relating to distance, but it does not measure distance and time of a moving object using simple equipment. It is a rule-of-thumb for storm distance, not a measurement activity for motion.

copy.en: Count the seconds from the flash to the thunder to guess the storm's distance! About three seconds means the storm is one kilometer away.
copy.tl: Bilangin mo ang mga segundo mula kidlat hanggang kulog para malaman ang layo ng bagyo! Mga tatlong segundo ay isang kilometro ang layo.
copy.bis: Ihap ang mga segundo gikan sa kilat hangtod sa dalugdog aron mahibaw-an ang gilay-on sa bagyo! Mga tulo ka segundo usa ka kilometro ang gilay-on.

Why should we always cover our food?

Covering food protects it from flies, dust, and microbes floating in the air!
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat nating laging takpan ang pagkain?

Ang pagtatakip sa pagkain ay nagpoprotekta dito mula sa langaw, alikabok, at mikrobyong nasa hangin!
copy.bis:
Nganong dapat kanunay natong tabunan ang pagkaon?

Ang pagtabon sa pagkaon nanalipod niini gikan sa langaw, abog, ug mikrobyo nga naglutaw sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cowbirds in other countries do the very same trick

copy.en: Cuckoos aren't the only birds that dump their eggs in other nests -- cowbirds in other countries do the very same trick.
copy.tl: Hindi lang ang cuckoo ang nangingitlog sa pugad ng iba -- ganito rin ang ginagawa ng cowbird sa ibang bansa.
copy.bis: Dili lang ang cuckoo ang mangitlog sa salag sa uban -- mao usab ang ginabuhat sa cowbird sa ubang nasod.

copy.en:
Why does a crab slow down in cold water?

Crabs are cold-blooded — their body temperature follows the surroundings. Cold makes them slow and rest; warmth makes them active again.
copy.tl:
Bakit bumabagal ang alimango sa malamig na tubig?

Cold-blooded ang alimango — sumusunod ang init ng katawan nito sa paligid. Pag malamig, bumabagal at nagpapahinga; pag mainit, aktibo ulit ito.
copy.bis:
Nganong mohinay ang alimango sa bugnaw nga tubig?

Cold-blooded ang alimango — ang init sa lawas niini nagsunod sa palibot. Kon bugnaw, mohinay ug mopahuway; kon init, mabalik kining aktibo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A crab has gills tucked inside its shell
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes gills, an internal respiratory organ, not outer body parts like head, legs, or wings, and does not address movement or food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: take in oxygen from water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen but does not identify basic needs such as air, food, water, or shelter as needs of living things.

copy.en:
How does a crab breathe?

A crab has gills tucked inside its shell that take in oxygen from water. As long as the gills stay damp, it can breathe out of water for a while—that's why you sometimes see it bubbling.
copy.tl:
Paano huminga ang alimango?

May mga hasang ang alimango sa loob ng talukab na sumisipsip ng oxygen mula sa tubig. Basta basa ang hasang, kaya rin nitong huminga sa lupa saglit, kaya minsan nakikita mong nagbubula ito.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghinga sa alimango?

Adunay hasang ang alimango sulod sa talukab nga mosuyop og oxygen gikan sa tubig. Basta basa ang hasang, makaginhawa pa kini sa yuta sa makadiyot, mao nga usahay makita nimong mubuga og bula kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Crab eyes are excellent at spotting movement.

Why does a crab shed its shell?

Hindi tumutugma sa paglaki ang matigas na balat ng alimango. Kaya para lumaki, kailangan nitong alisin ang lumang balat at gumawa ng mas malaki!

Can crickets tell you the temperature?

Medyo, oo! Mas mabilis kumuliglig ang kuliglig kapag mainit — may lumang formula na Dolbear's Law na tinatantya ang temperatura batay sa bilang ng kuliglig kada minuto.

What decides if a baby crocodile is male or female?

Not chromosomes but nest temperature! Certain warmth makes more male eggs hatch, other warmth makes more females.

Hindi ito chromosome kundi ang temperatura ng pugad! May tiyak na init na gumagawa ng mas maraming lalaki, at iba namang init na gumagawa ng mas maraming babae.

A single female crown-of-thorns starfish can produce over 60 million eggs in a year — when food is plentiful and predators are scarce, their numbers explode and can wreck huge reef areas within months!

Ang pinakamaraming element sa balat ng Daigdig (Earth's crust) ay oxygen! Hindi lang siya sa hangin, nasa mga bato at lupa rin!
